headline: Approved rezoning of 162 Washington Street from R2 to C1, $4485.22 in tax abatements, and a La Milonga Bar closure and probation agreement.
summary: Approved rezoning 162 Washington Street from R2 to C1 on a 5–0 roll call vote. Approved $4485.22 in tax abatements and a $315.42 tax addition for Pledge Financial RI. Approved an agreement requiring La Milonga Bar to close for three days and serve six months of probation.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 13, 2026 meeting as amended, 5–0.
Approved the appointment of Olivia Demanche to the Juvenile Hearing Board, 5–0.
Received the department financial reports for July-August 2026.
Approved the agreement requiring La Milonga Bar to close for three days and serve six months of probation, 5–0.
Tabled the peddler license for Yessenia Rodriguez, D/B/A One Fly Stop, 5–0.
Approved the Class A Restaurant license for La Receta Colombiana, 5–0.
Approved the Class C Variety license for Chapines Supermarket Inc., 5–0.
Approved the recommended tax abatements totaling $4485.22, 5–0.
Approved the $315.42 tax addition for Pledge Financial RI, 5–0.
Approved the ordinance rezoning 162 Washington Street from R2 to C1 on second reading, 5–0.
Referred the $6,005.67 claim by Bernice Hernandez to the Trust, 5–0.

a. Consideration of appointment by Mayor Maria Rivera of Olivia Demanche of N. 
Providence, to the Juvenile Hearing Board with a term set to expire September 1, 2029 
The Council may vote on this item 
Lorrain Quintero, Chief of Staff to Mayor Maria Rivera, addressed the Council and introduced Ms. Olivia 
Demanche, providing background information regarding her qualifications. Ms. Demanche then addressed 
the Council and responded to questions from the members. A motion to approve Ms. Demanche’s 
appointment to the Juvenile Hearing Board was made by Councilperson Baena and seconded by 
Councilperson Peguero. The motion passed unanimously, 5–0.

VII. New Business 
a. CDBG PRESENTATION 
i. Presentation by the Planning Director Jim Vandermillen regarding the Community 
Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program. 
Planning Director Jim Vandermillen addressed the Council and provided an overview of the Community 
Development Block Grant (CDBG) program, explaining its purpose, objectives, and intended use of funding. 
He discussed how the program supports community development initiatives and helps address local needs 
through eligible projects and activities. Director Vandermillen also provided context regarding the types of 
projects and services that could receive funding, emphasizing the program’s role in supporting community 
improvements and enhancing the quality of life for residents. 
 
 
b. City Council sitting as Board of License Commissioners  
i. Hearing and/or consideration and possible action regarding the following license 
and license holders Jesus Santos & Fernando Santos representing JFR &Son, LLC, 
D/B/A La Milonga Bar, 674 Dexter Streerty, Central Falls, RI 02863 holding a 
Class BV License. 
The Council may vote on this item 
City Solicitor Matthew Jerzyk addressed the Council and provided background regarding the incident at L 
Milonga Bar and Grill, during which two patrons were stabbed. Detective Aida Allen approached the podium 
and provided additional details regarding the events that occurred on the night of the violations. 
Councilperson Baena asked questions concerning the incident and the circumstances surrounding the 
violations. 
 
Solicitor Jerzyk informed the Council that an agreement had been reached between the City and the 
establishment’s legal counsel. Under the agreement, L Milonga Bar and Grill would be required to close for 
three days, with the closure scheduled to take place over a weekend. Additionally, the establishment would be 
placed on probation for a period of six months. 
 
A motion to approve the proposal presented by Solicitor Jerzyk was made by Councilperson Peguero and 
seconded by Councilperson Kazarian. Council President Pro Tempore Rivas Lugo called for a roll-call vote. 
Councilperson Baena voted yes, Councilperson Kazarian voted yes, Councilperson Peguero voted yes, 
Councilperson Rosado Martinez voted yes, and Council President Pro Tempore Rivas Lugo voted yes. The 
motion passed unanimously, 5–0.

      Schedule of Bills-Hearing and/or consideration 
a) An Ordinance Amending the Official Zoning Map to Rezone Certain Property Located at 
162 Washington Street from R2 to C1. SUB A (Councilperson Rivas Lugo by request)-
Second Reading 
The Council may vote on this item 
 
Council President Pro Tempore Alberto Rivas-Lugo opened the public hearing. As no members of the public 
had signed up to speak, the public hearing was subsequently closed. 
 
Under discussion, City Solicitor Jerzyk addressed the Council and provided background and context 
regarding the ordinance, including his legal opinion on the matter. A motion to approve the ordinance was 
made by Councilperson Peguero and seconded by Councilperson Rosado-Martinez. 
 
Council President Pro Tempore Rivas-Lugo called for a roll-call vote. Councilperson Baena voted yes, 
Councilperson Kazarian voted yes, Councilperson Peguero voted yes, Councilperson Rosado-Martinez voted 
yes, and Council President Pro Tempore Rivas-Lugo voted yes. The motion passed unanimously, 5–0. 
 
VIII. Hearing and/or Consideration of Claim 
i. Bernice Hernandez 
Central Falls, RI 02863 
Alleged damage to passenger side due to collision with police vehicle 
Estimated amount $6,005.67 
The Council may vote on this item 
 
Council President Pro Tempore Rivas-Lugo requested a motion to move Item VIII to the top of the agenda. 
A motion to move the item was made by Councilperson Kazarian and seconded by Councilperson Rosado-
Martinez. 
 
Under discussion, the Council determined that the damage exceeded the City’s insurance deductible. Based 
on the City Solicitor’s recommendation, a motion to refer the matter to the Trust was made by Councilperson 
Baena and seconded by Councilperson Peguero. The motion passed unanimously, 5–0. 
 
IX. Adjournment 
 
A motion to adjourn was made by Councilperson Peguero and seconded by Councilperson Rosado-Martinez. 
The meeting adjourned at 7:01 p.m.
